record_title: Exact two-prime-support criterion and a lower bound for lambda-star practical numbers
scientific_context: For a>=3, odd prime p and b>=1, lambda-star-practicality of 2^a p^b is classified by an explicit necessary-and-sufficient block-gap inequality. The b=1 case is equivalent to p <= 2^(a-1)+3 and yields F_{lambda*}(X) >= (1-o(1))*sqrt(X)/log(X).
limitations: The exact classification is restricted to integers of the form 2^a p^b with a>=3 and p odd prime. The resulting square-root-order lower bound does not settle the empirically suggested X/log X scale. Originality is to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk from literature using different terminology. The finite verification supports but does not replace the proof; no formal proof-assistant verification or independent audit is asserted.

artifact_inventory.description: Standalone direct complete-sequence verification of the 2^a p^b classification and the b=1 prime threshold on a finite parameter grid.
Deterministic output of the finite verification.
